page.title: The quickjs sandbox
page.description: Run charts your users upload in QuickJS, an engine inside the package that stops a runaway loop or allocation with an error.

hero.headline: Run charts you did not write
hero.lede: An uploaded chart runs in QuickJS, a separate engine inside the package, where a runaway loop ends in an error.

section.heading: Choose the engine for each host
section.p: A host runs all its charts' code in one engine, its datamodel, which the datamodel option picks.

item.text: Chart code runs in a node:vm context of your own engine, fast and with your engine's values. A vm context looks like a sandbox but is not one: a chart in it can reach your process.
Chart code runs in QuickJS, an engine compiled into the package. It has no modules, timers, files or network, and it stops an evaluation that runs too long or takes too much memory.

section.p: Give every chart you did not write a quickjs host: charts your users upload, and charts a program generates.

section.heading: Stop a chart that loops forever
section.p: This chart loops without end, allocates without end and looks for Node.js's globals. QuickJS stops both loops with error.execution, and finds no globals.

example.code: stopped: error.execution stopped: error.execution undefined undefined undefined

section.p: The actor handles error.execution like any other event, then goes on to its next one.

section.heading: Limit memory for the whole engine
section.p: The host's quickjs option sets the engine's limits. A host on the native datamodel refuses the option with a TypeError.

row.cell: the engine's interrupt checks one evaluation may make before it is stopped
bytes for the whole engine, every actor of the host together

'isolated' gives every actor a context of its own (below)

section.p: 40,000 resident actors take about 112 MB of engine heap, so the default of 1 GiB holds tens of thousands. Raise it for a host that keeps more actors resident.
host.quickjsHeapBytes reports the engine's heap, every actor's together, to watch against memoryLimit.

section.heading: Limit how long one evaluation runs
section.p: maxOps counts the engine's interrupt checks, one per 10,000 jumps and calls. How long one looping evaluation holds its thread at each setting:

table.caption: Every host on the thread waits that long. Measured 2026-10-18 on an Intel Xeon at 2.10 GHz, Linux; Node.js 22 and Bun 1.4.1 alike.

section.p: Set it by the stall your other actors can take: a few hundred for request handling, about 1000 for background work.
An evaluation that needs more checks than maxOps fails every time, so measure your charts' real work before you lower it.
The actor's _event.data.reason names the limit that stopped it: 'fuel' for maxOps, 'memory' for memoryLimit.

section.heading: Give each actor its own builtins
section.p: The actors of one chart share a context, so a chart that changes Array.prototype changes it for all of them. A chart whose scripts declare top-level names gets a context per actor.
With realm: 'isolated' every actor gets a context of its own, at the cost of its memory.

section.heading: Expect hibernation and values to differ
section.p: A chart behaves the same on both engines. Two things around it differ:

item.text: QuickJS writes its own values into a hibernated actor's blob, so a Date, Map, Set, typed array or graph with cycles comes back. A class's instance comes back as a plain object, and a function in a variable keeps the actor in memory ().

Event data and spawn params are converted to the engine's values and back through the value table. A key holding undefined is dropped and an array's undefined becomes null, where the native datamodel keeps both.

section.p: Most operations cost less on quickjs, and an idle actor takes less memory: Capacity and memory has the numbers.
